title: Gerunds and Infinitives
content:
Definition

English: Gerunds and Infinitives are verb forms used as nouns, subjects, or objects in a sentence instead of ordinary verbs.
Hindi: Gerund aur Infinitive aise verb roop hote hain jo vaakya mein sangya (noun), karta, ya karm ke roop mein prayog hoti hain.

Example: Reading is fun. / I want to read.
Hindi: पढ़ना मजेदार है। / मैं पढ़ना चाहता हूँ.

title: What is a Gerund?
content:
Explanation

English: A Gerund is a verb + ing form that functions as a noun.
Hindi: Gerund ek aisi kriya hoti hai jisme verb ke saath 'ing' lagakar use noun ki tarah prayog kiya jata hai.

  • Always ends with –ing (reading, playing, swimming).
  • Acts like a noun (subject or object).
Examples:
1. Reading books is my hobby. → किताबें पढ़ना मेरा शौक है।
2. She enjoys singing. → उसे गाना पसंद है।
3. He is afraid of flying. → उसे उड़ने से डर लगता है।

title: What is an Infinitive?
content:
Explanation

English: An Infinitive is the base form of a verb with 'to', showing purpose or intention.
Hindi: Infinitive kriya ka aadhar roop hota hai jisme 'to' lagaya jata hai; yeh uddeshya ya irada batata hai.

  • Form: to + base verb (to go, to eat, to play)
  • Shows purpose, plan, or reason.
Examples:
1. I like to sing. → मुझे गाना पसंद है।
2. She wants to travel. → वह यात्रा करना चाहती है।
3. He came to help me. → वह मेरी मदद करने आया।

title: Gerund vs Infinitive
content:
Comparison

English: Both can act as subjects or objects but are used differently depending on verbs or context.
Hindi: Dono sangya ke roop mein kaam karte hain, lekin unka prayog verb aur sandarbh par nirbhar karta hai.

AspectGerundInfinitive
FormVerb + ing (e.g., swimming)To + verb (e.g., to swim)
UseExpresses activity as a conceptExpresses purpose or intent
ExampleI enjoy reading.I want to read.
Hindiक्रिया-संज्ञा (पढ़ना)उद्देश्य बताने वाला रूप (पढ़ना)

title: Verbs Followed by Gerunds
content:
Use

English: Some verbs are always followed by gerunds.
Hindi: Kuch kriyaen sadhaaran roop se gerund ke saath prayukt hoti hain.

  • Enjoy – I enjoy reading.
  • Avoid – He avoids smoking.
  • Finish – She finished writing.
  • Admit – He admitted cheating.
  • Suggest – I suggested going there.
Hindi: Aisi kriyaen जिनके baad hamेशा 'verb + ing' form aata hai.

title: Verbs Followed by Infinitives
content:
Use

English: Some verbs are followed by infinitives.
Hindi: Kuch kriyaen sadhaaran roop se infinitive ke saath prayukt hoti hain.

  • Decide – He decided to go.
  • Plan – We plan to visit Delhi.
  • Want – I want to learn.
  • Hope – They hope to win.
  • Forget – Don’t forget to call.
Hindi: Aisi kriyaen जिनके baad hamेशा 'to + verb' form aata hai.

title: Verbs Used with Both
content:
Explanation

English: Some verbs can take either a gerund or infinitive with a change in meaning.
Hindi: Kuch kriyaen gerund aur infinitive dono ke saath aa sakti hain, par arth badal jata hai.

  • Stop –
    'He stopped smoking.' (He quit smoking.)
    'He stopped to smoke.' (He stopped another activity in order to smoke.)
  • Remember –
    'I remember meeting him.' (Memory of the past.)
    'Remember to meet him.' (Future reminder.)
  • Try –
    'Try turning it on.' (Experiment.)
    'Try to turn it on.' (Make an effort.)

title: Common Mistakes
content:
Explanation

English: Learners often confuse verbs that require -ing or to + verb forms.
Hindi: Seekhne waale aksar bhool karte hain ki kis verb ke baad gerund ya infinitive aana chahiye.

Wrong: I enjoy to play football.
Correct: I enjoy playing football.
Wrong: I want going home.
Correct: I want to go home.
